headline: Praised, not impeached
dek: The President attacks Congressman Thomas Massie for seeking to impeach the Secretary of War, Pete Hegseth, and asks Congress to stand up for him, citing record recruitment and “two victories”, Venezuela and Iran.

original.speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Defeated Republican Congressman Thomas Massie, a total loser, is trying to Impeach perhaps the most popular and successful military official in the Country, Secretary of War, Pete Hegseth. With recruitment at an ALL-TIME HIGH, from an all-time low under Sleepy Joe Biden, and TWO VICTORIES, Venezuela and Iran, Pete Hegseth should be praised, not Impeached. Congress, stand up for Pete!!! President DJT
original.context: Posted on the evening of 9 November 2026. Thomas Massie is a Republican congressman from Kentucky. Since 2025, the Department of Defense has also used the name Department of War, and its head the title Secretary of War.

verification.note: Copied by the editor from truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump on 10 November 2026 (shown as Nov 09, 2026, 5:36 PM Pacific).

en: I strongly disagree with Congressman Thomas Massie’s effort to impeach the Secretary of War, Pete Hegseth.

In my view, the Secretary deserves credit: my administration reports that military recruitment has recovered strongly, and he has overseen our operations in Venezuela and Iran. I ask Congress to stand with him.
fr: Je désapprouve fermement la démarche du représentant Thomas Massie, qui veut engager une procédure de destitution contre le secrétaire à la Guerre, Pete Hegseth.

À mes yeux, le secrétaire mérite d’être salué : selon mon administration, le recrutement militaire s’est nettement redressé, et il a dirigé nos opérations au Venezuela et en Iran. Je demande au Congrès de le soutenir.

fribourgeois.hook: À la désalpe, toutes les vaches redescendent. *Record absolu.*
fribourgeois.hookEn: At the cattle descent, every cow comes home. *An all-time record.*
text: Le député Thomas Massie, battu, un vrai perdant, veut destituer peut-être le militaire le plus populaire du pays : Pete Hegseth, mon secrétaire à la Guerre. Recrutement au plus haut, deux victoires, le Venezuela et l’Iran : c’est moi qui vous le dis.

Chez nous, en Gruyère, à la désalpe, toutes les vaches redescendent de l’alpage, fleuries : record absolu, chaque année. Et personne n’a jamais proposé de destituer l’armailli. Alors, le Congrès, soutenez Pete comme on soutient un armailli : avec des cloches, et en chantant.
en: Congressman Thomas Massie, beaten, a real loser, wants to impeach perhaps the most popular military man in the country: Pete Hegseth, my Secretary of War. Recruitment at an all-time high, two victories, Venezuela and Iran: you heard it from me.

Round here, in the Gruyère, at the cattle descent, every cow comes down from the mountain pasture, decked with flowers: an all-time record, every year. And nobody has ever suggested impeaching the herdsman. So, Congress, stand up for Pete the way we stand up for a herdsman: with cowbells, and singing.
notes: The désalpe (or poya) is the autumn descent of the herds from the Alpine pastures, the cows decked with flowers and bells. The armailli is the herdsman of the Gruyère, whose song, the Ranz des vaches, is Fribourg’s unofficial anthem.

vaudois.hook: Davel a eu sa statue. *Il a juste fallu attendre 175 ans.*
vaudois.hookEn: Davel got his statue. *We only had to wait 175 years.*
text: Le député Thomas Massie, qui a été battu, pas un gagnant, quoi, veut destituer Pete Hegseth, mon secrétaire à la Guerre, peut-être le militaire le plus populaire du pays. Le recrutement au plus haut, deux victoires, le Venezuela et l’Iran : moi, je dis qu’il faudrait plutôt le féliciter.

Remarquez, chez nous, on n’est pas pressés. Le Major Davel, Berne l’a exécuté en 1723, et nous, on lui a fait une statue en 1898. Alors, féliciter Pete, on verra bien. Mais le destituer, ça presse pas non plus. Le Congrès, soutenez-le, tranquillement.
en: Congressman Thomas Massie, who was beaten, not exactly a winner, wants to impeach Pete Hegseth, my Secretary of War, perhaps the most popular military man in the country. Recruitment at an all-time high, two victories, Venezuela and Iran: I say we should be congratulating him instead.

Mind you, round here we’re never in a hurry. Major Davel was executed by Bern in 1723, and we put up his statue in 1898. So congratulating Pete, we’ll see. But impeaching him, there’s no rush either. Congress, stand by him, nice and easy.
notes: Major Davel led an attempt to free Vaud from Bernese rule and was executed in 1723; he became the hero of the canton, and his statue stands in front of the Château Saint-Maire in Lausanne since 1898.

lyonnais.hook: Quand un gone travaille bien, *on lui paye un mâchon, pas un procès.*
lyonnais.hookEn: When a lad does a good job, *you buy him breakfast, not a trial.*
text: Le député Thomas Massie, un battu, un vrai perdant, veut destituer Pete Hegseth, mon secrétaire à la Guerre, peut-être le militaire le plus populaire du pays. Le recrutement au plus haut, deux victoires, le Venezuela et l’Iran : moi, je dis qu’il faut le féliciter.

À Lyon, quand un gone fait du bon travail, on ne lui fait pas un procès : on lui paye un mâchon, à neuf heures du matin, saucisson chaud, cervelle de canut et un petit beaujolais. Le Congrès, venez donc avec nous : soutenez Pete, et apportez le pain.
en: Congressman Thomas Massie, a loser, a real loser, wants to impeach Pete Hegseth, my Secretary of War, perhaps the most popular military man in the country. Recruitment at an all-time high, two victories, Venezuela and Iran: I say he deserves congratulations.

In Lyon, when a lad does a good job, you don’t put him on trial: you buy him a proper Lyon breakfast at nine in the morning, hot sausage, herbed cheese and a glass of Beaujolais. Congress, come and join us: stand up for Pete, and bring the bread.
notes: The mâchon is the hearty mid-morning meal of Lyon’s silk workers, the canuts; “cervelle de canut” (“silk worker’s brain”) is a fresh cheese with herbs. “Gone” is Lyon slang for a kid, or a fellow Lyonnais.

parisien.hook: Napoléon dort aux Invalides. *Personne n’est venu le destituer.*
parisien.hookEn: Napoleon sleeps at Les Invalides. *Nobody has come to impeach him.*
text: Le député Thomas Massie, battu, un loser total, veut destituer Pete Hegseth, mon secrétaire à la Guerre, peut-être le militaire le plus populaire du pays. Recrutement record, deux victoires, le Venezuela et l’Iran, c’est moi qui le dis, et lui, il veut le virer ?

À Paris, nos militaires, on les met aux Invalides, sous un dôme doré. Napoléon y repose depuis 1840, et personne n’est venu le destituer. Bon, il avait déjà abdiqué, mais quand même. Le Congrès, soutenez Pete. Et dépêchez-vous, il y a la queue.
en: Congressman Thomas Massie, beaten, a total loser, wants to impeach Pete Hegseth, my Secretary of War, perhaps the most popular military man in the country. Record recruitment, two victories, Venezuela and Iran, I’m the one saying it, and he wants to fire him?

In Paris, we put our soldiers in Les Invalides, under a golden dome. Napoleon has rested there since 1840, and nobody has come to impeach him. All right, he had already abdicated, but still. Congress, stand up for Pete. And hurry up, there’s a queue.
notes: Les Invalides, built by Louis XIV for wounded soldiers, houses France’s army museum; Napoleon’s remains were brought back from Saint Helena in 1840 and lie under its golden dome.

new-york.hook: Two victories? That’s a ticker-tape parade. *Not a hearing.*
text: Thomas Massie, a defeated congressman, a total loser, wants to impeach Pete Hegseth, my Secretary of War, maybe the most popular military guy in the country. Recruitment? All-time high, I’m telling you. Two victories, Venezuela and Iran.

In New York, two victories get you a ticker-tape parade down the Canyon of Heroes. Confetti, the works. Not a hearing. Congress, stand up for Pete. And somebody call Sanitation, we’re gonna need them.
en: He attacks the congressman who wants to impeach his Secretary of War, and repeats his own claims: record recruitment and two victories, in Venezuela and Iran.

In New York, heroes and winning teams get a ticker-tape parade along lower Broadway, the “Canyon of Heroes”; the city’s Sanitation Department then sweeps up the paper. A parade, he says, not a congressional hearing.

deep-south.hook: Down here we give a soldier a pound cake. *Not an impeachment.*
text: Now, that Thomas Massie, who just lost, poor thing, wants to impeach Pete Hegseth, my Secretary of War, the most popular military man in the country, if you ask me. Recruitment’s at an all-time high, I’m told, and we’ve had two victories, Venezuela and Iran.

Down here, when a man serves his country, we give him a parade, a pound cake and a seat on the porch. We don’t impeach him. That’s just bad manners. Congress, stand up for Pete, and mind your manners.
en: With exaggerated sympathy (“poor thing”), he dismisses the congressman who wants to impeach his Secretary of War, and repeats the claims of record recruitment and two victories.
In the South, he says, you thank a serviceman with a parade, homemade cake and Southern hospitality; impeaching him would be a breach of good manners.

liverpool.hook: Two trophies and they want him sacked? *You’ll never walk alone, Pete.*
text: Thomas Massie, lad, who got beaten, a proper loser, and now he wants Pete Hegseth impeached. My Secretary of War! Most popular military fella in the country, I reckon. Recruitment’s never been higher, I’m telling you, and two wins: Venezuela and Iran.
Round here, a manager who brings home two trophies gets his name sung on the Kop. You don’t sack him. So come on, Congress, stand up for Pete. You’ll never walk alone, lad.
en: He dismisses the congressman as a loser, calls his Secretary of War the country’s most popular military official, and repeats his claims of record recruitment and two “wins”.
In Liverpool, a football manager who wins trophies is celebrated by the fans on the Kop, Anfield’s famous stand, not fired; “You’ll Never Walk Alone” is the club’s anthem.

british-diplomat.hook: Congress may disagree. *That is rather the point of Congress.*
text: His Majesty’s Government notes with interest the debate in Congress concerning the Secretary of War, and the title itself: our own War Office became the Ministry of Defence in 1964, and we have grown rather attached to the more modest name.
Ministers in our Parliament are questioned regularly, sometimes uncomfortably, and generally survive the experience. We wish Congress a productive discussion.
en: He likes his Secretary of War.
Congress may disagree. That is rather the point of Congress.

text: France follows the debates of the American Congress with the greatest respect.

It was a Frenchman, Montesquieu, who wrote that power must check power, and the authors of the American Constitution read him closely. We are always moved to see the idea still at work, even when it is inconvenient for someone.
fr: La France suit les débats du Congrès américain avec le plus grand respect.

C’est un Français, Montesquieu, qui a écrit qu’il faut que le pouvoir arrête le pouvoir, et les auteurs de la Constitution américaine l’ont lu de près. Nous sommes toujours émus de voir l’idée encore à l’œuvre, même lorsqu’elle dérange quelqu’un.
notes: In “The Spirit of the Laws” (1748), Montesquieu argued that “power must check power”; James Madison cites him in the Federalist Papers when defending the separation of powers.

text: The Federal Council takes note of this debate.

In Switzerland, the department in charge of the army is also responsible for civil protection and for sport. No one has ever tried to impeach its head: our law does not provide for it, and the Federal Council takes its decisions together, so there would be seven people to impeach. We find it simpler to hold a vote.
fr: Le Conseil fédéral prend acte de ce débat.

En Suisse, le département chargé de l’armée s’occupe aussi de la protection de la population et du sport. Personne n’a jamais tenté d’en destituer le chef : notre droit ne le prévoit pas, et le Conseil fédéral décide collégialement, si bien qu’il faudrait destituer sept personnes. Nous trouvons plus simple de voter.
notes: The Swiss army falls under the Federal Department of Defence, Civil Protection and Sport. Federal councillors are elected for four years and cannot be removed during their term; the seven-member Federal Council governs collegially.
